messages.subject: Quadratic form for GMRF precision
parts:
Hi all,

TMB and RTMB include helpful functions to calculate the density function for a GMRF given a sparse precision Q.  However, in many cases (e.g., the SPDE method or nearest neighbor GP) the precision Q results from a quadratic form Q = (I-G^T) D (I-G) where I is an identity matrix, D is a diagonal matrix, and G is a sparse path matrix.

Has anyone compared the efficiency of the built-in GMRF density functions against alternative calculations that use the quadratic form, i.e., calculating the det(Q) vs. det(I-G)^2 \times det(D)?  

Cheers,
Jim
